preheader: 29 books reviewed in the British papers this week, fiction and non-fiction, one line each.

books.author: Joe Biden
books.subject: Politics & world affairs
books.line: The former president's memoir of policy wins and battles with Trump, which skirts his failed re-election bid.

books.author: Sonia Gandhi
books.subject: Biography & memoir
books.line: The Italian-born kingmaker of Indian politics tells her own story after years of silence.
books.why: An Italian outsider who became the power broker of the world's largest democracy.

books.author: Haruki Murakami
books.subject: Biography & memoir
books.line: The novelist traces the life of his estranged father, from adoption and abandonment to the horrors of the second world war.
books.why: A famous novelist uncovering his estranged father's wartime past.

books.author: Philip Ball
books.subject: Biography & memoir
books.line: A portrait of the physicist Niels Bohr, explaining his discoveries and the passion that drove them.

books.author: Kate Wilson
books.subject: Espionage
books.line: An account of the undercover policing scandal, in which officers lied in court and deceived women into relationships.
books.why: Undercover officers living double lives inside protest groups, and the women they deceived.

books.book: Weimar: Life on the Edge of Catastrophe
books.author: Katja Hoyer
books.subject: History
books.line: A history of Germany's Weimar years, the fragile democracy that ended in Nazism.

books.book: Pax Economica: Left-Wing Visions of a Free Trade World
books.author: Marc-William Palen
books.subject: History
books.line: How liberals, radicals, feminists and others on the left have championed free trade since the mid-19th century.

books.book: Becoming Arab: The Formation of Arab Identity in the Medieval Middle East
books.author: Yossef Rapoport
books.subject: History
books.line: How Arab identity took shape in the centuries after the rise of Islam.

books.book: Up in the Air: A History of High-Rise Britain
books.author: Holly Smith
books.subject: History
books.line: The story of the council tower blocks built for working-class tenants across postwar Britain.

books.author: A.J.A. Woods
books.subject: Society & ideas
books.line: Why the right blames the Frankfurt School for the decline of the West, and where the theory comes from.

books.book: The Frenchmen: Or, My Life in Theory
books.author: Emily Eakin
books.subject: Society & ideas
books.line: An account of the French theorists who fought each other in public over the biggest ideas of their day.

books.author: Ben Dark
books.subject: Nature & place
books.line: A gardener's natural history of the plant dynasties that dominate the green world.

books.author: Geoffrey Grigson
books.subject: Nature & place
books.line: A poetic guide to British wild plants, full of myth and folklore.

books.author: Daniel Simberloff
books.subject: Nature & place
books.line: A history of biological invasions and of the science that grew up to study them.

books.author: Sam Wasson
books.subject: Arts & culture
books.line: How the director of It's a Wonderful Life built his name on films of the little man against the system.
books.why: The Hollywood director who sold America its own dream, and the man behind the myth.

books.author: Louis Shadwick
books.subject: Arts & culture
books.line: A life of the painter of urban loneliness, and of the wife he could not have done without.

books.book: Clint: The Man and the Movies
books.author: Shawn Levy
books.subject: Arts & culture
books.line: A biography of Clint Eastwood and the films that made him.

books.book: A Chorus of Ears: On 'the Voice of the Poem'
books.author: Denise Riley
books.subject: Books & writing
books.line: The poet asks what lyric voice is made of and what it is like inside a poet's head.

books.author: Gary Shteyngart
books.subject: Life & leisure
books.line: The novelist celebrates the small pleasures, from martinis to capybara videos, that bring him joy.

books.author: Nick Harkaway
books.subject: Crime & thriller fiction
books.line: A new thriller from Nick Harkaway.

books.author: Mick Herron
books.subject: Crime & thriller fiction
books.line: A new thriller from Mick Herron.

books.author: Stephanie Wrobel
books.subject: Crime & thriller fiction
books.line: A new thriller from Stephanie Wrobel.

books.author: Nicola Upson
books.subject: Crime & thriller fiction
books.line: A new crime novel from Nicola Upson.

books.author: Annie Proulx
books.subject: Literary fiction
books.line: A collection of short stories from the author of Brokeback Mountain.

books.author: Chad Harbach
books.subject: Literary fiction
books.line: Fifteen years on, a follow-up to The Art of Fielding about female friendship and the mess of early adulthood.

books.author: Andrea Bajani
books.subject: Literary fiction
books.line: A short Italian novel, translated by Geoffrey Brock, about family and its hold on the self.

books.author: Joan Barfoot
books.subject: Literary fiction
books.line: A reissued feminist novel imagining a sparer life for a woman outside the nuclear family.

books.author: Dimosthenis Papamarkos
books.subject: Historical fiction
books.line: Linked stories of ambushes and vendettas in the bitter Greco-Turkish war of 1919-22, newly translated.
books.why: Ambushes and blood feuds in a little-known war, told through linked lives.

books.author: Bob Mortimer
books.subject: Other fiction
books.line: The comedian's novel about a troubled teenager in 1970s Middlesbrough.
